notes.title: Devlog 10: Narrative and Game Design changes.
notes.content:
Hello Goodlanders! In this devlog we share some of the upcoming changes to our game and current prototyping experiments.

News:
* The playtest is closed now! Thank you so much for the eye-opening feedback and excellent suggestions.
* We've finalized two mini-games and plan to present the first one next week.

Upcoming
* More narrative choices for core-loop mechanics - acquire, build chain, upgrade and protect a business. 
Rewritten demo scenes with the focus on Mr Harwood's perspective.
* Made UI easier to read, we decided to increase the text size in Facebook messages and event cards. 

Prototyping & Researching
* We experiment with management mechanics to launder money by maximizing efficiency and minimizing FBI infamy gain. 
* To launder money, a business will need to have dirty money. To send dirty money player will either need to transfer it by himself (in a mini-game where he needs to outsmart cops and not get into any roadblocks) or send someone of his crew (with lesser chances of success)

notes.title: Devlog 9: Upcoming features and new mini-games.
notes.content:
Hello Goodlanders! It is the last week of the open playtest.  We've got plenty of insightful feedback. Right now, we are processing it all and compiling the plan to improve the identified issues. 

News: 
* Our primary focus is to create fun mini-games to spice up the core gameplay loop. One of the games is to deliver/collect dirty cash between acquired businesses. 
* We extended the team and hired a narrative designer to improve the story delivery to give you more compelling choices and the immersive experience of living the money launderer life. 

The next Demo version will have:
* Reworked narrative and scenes
* Plenty of new compelling choices
* New mini-game to deliver/collect dirty cash between acquired businesses
* New sounds and ambients
* UI improvements

notes.title: Devlog 6: Welcome to the playtest!
notes.content:
Hello, bandits!

We, Big City Lab, are refining a demo version of our upcoming game, Welcome to Goodland.
So far we are not ready to publish it to a wide audience, but we really need to get the opinion of the players about the current state of the game, get feedback, and make the demo and the total game as well as possible. If you are ready to help us and take part in the closed playtest, we will be very grateful! Playtest will be open till November, 19th.

To participate, you need to follow these steps:
1. Go to the Welcome to Goodland Steam page.
https://store.steampowered.com/app/1724540/Welcome_to_Goodland/
2. Find the section that says “Join the Welcome to Goodland Playtest” and click on Request Access:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41151303/b14b1d372b010a3eb9f68b36a2e047dd90014955.png

3. Go to your Steam library, find Welcome to Goodland Playtest, download it and start the game.

After that, you can go through the playtest version. At the end of the walkthrough, please leave your feedback in one of the convenient ways:

 in the Steam Discussions
 on our Discord server
 in the survey

notes.title: Devlog 5: SFX, analytics
notes.content:
Good day!

We have decided to temporarily close the demo in order to provide you with an improved demo when ready. Of course, we do not stop working on the development of both the demo and the main game and will continue to keep you updated on development.

This week we worked on implementing cutscenes in the main game and introducing analytics into the game.

Analytics
Welcome to Goodland has a lot of both economic and moral and ethical decisions. It's difficult to predict the player’s behaviour, to understand what can be difficult and what is too easy. With the help of analytics, we will be able to more accurately understand which choices and businesses are more popular, which characters the players like more, at which moments the player experiences the greatest difficulties.

Sound effects
Also, now we are adding sounds to cutscenes, making them more dynamic and interesting. To do this, we use several steps:

 adding movement to cutscenes
 use transparency change
 move static cutscenes along the axes, while rotating the images
 add dashes to action scenes
 add visual effects (like gunshots) to action scenes


Along with this, we continue to work on sound and musical accompaniment. We added sounds of the city: ambient, noise of people and cars, howling of dogs ... Now, most actions are accompanied by effects: shots, hits, footsteps, engine roar, echoes of small objects, and so on.

Improvement of UI
We also continue to improve the clarity and readability of the interface. Initially, we wanted to provide the player with as much information as possible in the business capture menu, but we decided that the abundance of numbers could confuse the player. As a result, we left the required minimum, and additional data is now displayed by pressing key I.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41151303/9ee9a69c1cc7247d9de583a87abd0a9a1c8246be.png

Trailer
Another part of the development was the creation of a new trailer covering the game, mechanics and setting. Our task was to create an atmospheric and high-quality product, so we selected actors carefully, looking for voices that were as similar as possible to the characters we had invented. The hardest part was finding actors with a Mexican accent, as not that widespread. But in the end, we were pleased with the results of the preparation, and after a while, we will present you with a new trailer.

notes.title: Devlog 4: Demo update - tutorial, plot and SFX
notes.content:
Hello! Today we released a weekly demo update. What’s new:


 Updated tutorial
 Dynamic hints
 Updated cutscenes
 Added sound effects
 Fixed bugs

How we came to each of the decisions, in more detail:

Tutorial
We received a lot of feedback on the tutorial: the players complained it was too confusing and too long, and we fixed this important point.
First, we made the training interactive: the player learns new information during the game, during the exploration of new functionality, after meeting new mechanics, and at his own discretion.

To do this, we have implemented a couple of systems. The first is interactive notifications. At the beginning of the game, a bunch of messages no longer appear: now the player can choose himself when he needs to learn new info about the game. We have also introduced a system of triggers for certain actions: thanks to it, the player always receives updated information about the UI elements.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41151303/79398f409f3827be8f1c268a9e40fc93d3d2cc2c.gif

Plot
We also added more plot and moral choices. There are four endings in the game, which depend on the decisions and success of the player. Besides the endings, we added and improved the existing choices: we updated the visual, the description, and sometimes completely redesigned it, considering new situations.

SFX
One of the most important updates this week is sound. Player actions now have sound effects based on success or failure. In negotiations with business managers, this will help to better understand the result and feel the consequences.

notes.title: Devlog 3: the graphics
notes.content:
We do a lot of graphics for our game: we have cutscenes, character icons, business icons, a map, a solution screen, and more. Today we will tell you about the process of making graphics, the difficulties of development, and our criteria.

Character Portraits

Characters are an important part of our game, so we pay special attention to them.
Before we create a portrait of a character, we think about his character, his features, his visual characteristics and his role in the plot. We choose references from games and movies, make many sketches with different options for images and finally choose what best fits his image.

Once we decide on the character's image, we experiment with small visual details: jewellery, clothing, tattoos, and more.

In the final phase, we solicit feedback from the team: We ask team members if they remember the character, what design elements are most striking, what can be improved, what's missing, and so on. We make the final changes and add the portraits to the game.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41151303/c242175048fa17a3087844df448181d3bca44b5f.gif

Cutscenes

When creating cutscenes, we take inspiration from classic crime films like Ozark or Breaking Bad as well as noir or similar games: for example, This is the Police.

When creating cutscenes, we spend most of our time creating stylish and memorable scenes, compositions and images. First, we prepare the text, compose the plot, design a storyboard; then we draw the first versions of the cutscenes and insert them into the game after the improvements. Maybe the cutscenes are the most difficult part of the artistic development because of the variability and the additional implementation in the engine.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41151303/5039216f5d1389112a585f8aa9372d2aeb068adf.png

Icons

In a game from the genre of strategic management, you can not do without many small but very important icons on the screen.

When designing icons, the main thing is that they are easy to read in small sizes, which makes it difficult to add a lot of details.

Despite this (and maybe because of this), icons are the easiest element to produce art. In the screenshot below, you can see the options we chose from for each icon.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41151303/11db306302553c497cf149a277c515d4a60da287.png

notes.title: Devlog 2: Weekly Demo Update!
notes.content:
Hello!

This week we focused on updating the demo and improving the perspicuity of the game.

First, we have updated the display of morale changes in the decision menu. Previously, all results were displayed, but it was inconvenient for players to perceive a sizeable amount of information. We’ve added more animations, pictures and other elements to make information easier to read. The change in morale is now displayed on the character screen when you hover over one action.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41151303/cbcca41793404c4c6d45cfea6fdca35f39650469.gif

In addition, we also simplified the demo and the first chapters of the game. To do this, we have reduced the number of complex mechanics, changed the balance of the beginning of the game, and removed the cost change. We want the player to first learn how to manage a team, understand the UI, and take over businesses. The focus for the player should find a profitable business and building business chains.

One of the main current art tasks is to change the existing map of the city. We make many prototypes, experiment with the look and style of the city, the functionality of buildings and infrastructure. One factor that determines the visual of the city is the UI: interactive objects must be in the central part of the screen and not go beyond any UI element, otherwise, business elements cannot be captured, since they will be behind the interface layer.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41151303/eb1438ac93e817a3bcc17ac359000f20bf5dee15.png

We also drew and added new icons of bandits and bikers, business icons, and started the adding of cutscenes. In the demo version, we will show the main characters, three cutscenes and several interesting choices and situations.

Today’s new features and changes full list:



 system of cards-selections
 new cutscenes 
 the plot and action decisions 
 4 endings, depending on the character’s actions 
 the balance has changed
 updated icons of businesses
 updated characters
 UI of the main screen changed
 UI of the businesses changed 
 updated localization



Thank you for your feedback, it helps us a lot!

notes.title: Devlog 1: DevGamm Moscow and the first demo update!
notes.content:
Hey!

We were at DevGamm in Moscow to playtest the game, gather feedback, make connections and show the game to publishers.

And we got a lot of useful feedback on different aspects of the game: UI, design, art style... From this feedback, we have identified what works well and what needs to be improved or changed.

By making changes quickly, we update the demo taking into account the feedback received on DevGamm:


 Originally, we had planned to display attacks on businesses with pop-up icons and animations. However, we found that this method was not visible to players, they either did not notice this animation or clicked through.
So we decided to display the combat animation in separate windows. But in this case, it was not clear which businesses were attacked. So we moved the businesses under attack to the center, and the details of each attack are now displayed on the edges of the map.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41151303/39dce37526d932789513ca9643506dfec96fa933.gif
 Another problem with UI was the imperceptible formation of business chains. Originally, information about business chains had to be searched for in a separate window, and the chains themselves were only marked with lines.
In the new version, after a chain is formed, information about it appears in the upper right corner of the screen (this information is also displayed when you hover over the display panel). Businesses in chains are now highlighted to make the chain effect more visible.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41151303/9d955b298bbb84e26a83826af72deea1153d3d1d.gif

 Also, minor bugs and errors in the Russian localization have been fixed as part of the update.


We are waiting for your feedback in Steam discussions, on our Discord server or in our questionnaire.
Thank you for playing and sharing your impressions with us!
